description: canonical_bytes(subject) for subject.email/1 (verifier-toolkit/1 §8.5 + subject.email/1 §11): operate on RAW bytes (subject context is opaque per CCCP/1 §6.2). Step 1 (§11.2): global line-ending normalization to CRLF (single left-to-right pass, CRLF longest-match). Step 2 (§11.3): split at the FIRST CRLF CRLF (the 4-byte delimiter is removed from both sides); if absent, the whole message is headers and body is empty; a message beginning with CRLF CRLF has empty headers. Step 3 (§11.4): unfold headers ONLY as in RFC 5322 §2.2.3 -- each CRLF immediately followed by a WSP byte (SP 0x20 or HTAB 0x09) is deleted (CRLF removed, the following WSP preserved byte-for-byte, including SP-vs-HTAB identity and run length); order/names/values otherwise preserved. Step 4 (§11.5): body trailing-terminator normalization -- if body non-empty, strip its trailing run of CRLFs and append exactly one CRLF; empty body stays empty. Step 5 (§11.6): assemble headers_unfolded || CRLF CRLF || body_terminated, delimiter ALWAYS present. Canonicalization is idempotent. subject_local_digest_hex = SHA3-256(canonical_bytes).
canonicalization: §11.2 global CRLF normalization -> §11.3 split at first CRLF CRLF -> §11.4 unfold headers (RFC 5322: delete CRLF-before-WSP, preserve WSP) -> §11.5 body trailing-terminator normalization (non-empty body ends in exactly one CRLF) -> §11.6 headers || CRLF CRLF || body
digest: subject_local_digest_hex = SHA3-256(canonical_bytes), 32 bytes lowercase hex; verifier-local, never published
byte_notation: input_hex and canonical_hex are space-free lowercase hex of the raw byte sequence; 'A' = 0x41, ':' = 0x3a, 'b'=0x62, etc.

vectors.name: LF-only delimiter normalized to CRLF (same canonical)
no delimiter -> headers only, empty body, delimiter appended
folded header (CRLF SP) unfolds by deleting CRLF; the SP is preserved
folded header at HTAB: CRLF deleted, HTAB preserved (RFC 5322 unfolding)
folded multi-WSP run (SP SP HTAB): CRLF deleted, whole WSP run preserved
empty headers (message begins with CRLF CRLF)
3 CRLFs: only first CRLF CRLF is delimiter; body 'CRLF c' gains one trailing CRLF
empty input (0 bytes): empty headers, empty body, delimiter only
lone CR CR -> two line breaks -> delimiter
LF CR -> two line breaks, not one
double-conversion CR CR LF: each becomes two CRLFs; header B:c reclassified as body
folded header, no delimiter: whole input is headers
fold run truncated by end of headers (CRLF SP then delimiter)
SP after the delimiter belongs to the body; no unfolding across the delimiter
idempotence: a value already produced by this profile canonicalizes to itself

must_hold: global line-ending normalization runs before the split and applies to the whole message including the body; it reconciles single line breaks each represented as one of CR, LF, or CRLF, and does NOT reconcile a double conversion that represents one break as CR CR LF
split at the FIRST CRLF CRLF; the 4-byte delimiter is removed; further CRLFs belong to the body

unfolding applies to headers only and is RFC 5322 §2.2.3 unfolding: delete each CRLF immediately followed by a WSP byte and PRESERVE that WSP (SP or HTAB) unchanged; the WSP is neither collapsed nor rewritten; never unfold across the delimiter
body trailing-terminator normalization applies to the body only: a non-empty body ends in exactly one CRLF (trailing CRLF run collapsed, or one appended if absent); an empty body stays empty
final assembly always inserts exactly CRLF CRLF between headers and body, even when headers or body are empty
canonicalization is idempotent: re-canonicalizing a canonical value reproduces it
